extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of art history and classical literature; writers describing mythic/ancient subjects
extracted.subtask_description: Writing or critiquing descriptive, analytical prose about ancient Greek sculpture and myth, emphasizing how form, gesture, iconography and local context convey meaning and feeling. Also relevant to creative writers seeking to evoke mythic figures and provincial ancient life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monumental Homeric presence / combined solemnity and pathos
rubrics_metrics.description: Sculpture (e.g., Demeter) should be 'penetrated' with the sentiment of the Homeric hymn: uniting 'a certain solemnity of attitude and bearing' with 'a profound piteousness, an unrivalled pathos of expression.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gesture, bearing, and facial expression to evoke both monumental (Homeric) dignity and intimate human suffering. The text compares this pathos to 'the pity of Michelangelo's mater dolorosa' and notes expressive devices such as eyes 'represented as looking upwards' (contrary to usual ancient practice) to intensify emotional appeal. Aim to make the sorrow of the figure appear to have 'passed into the marble.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Drapery, fold-direction and proportion to convey type
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportions and treatment of drapery should signal character: e.g., 'tall figure, in proportion above the ordinary height, is veiled, and clad to the feet in the longer tunic, its numerous folds hanging in heavy parallel lines, opposing the lines of the peplus, or cloak, which cross it diagonally over the breast.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose folds (parallel vs diagonal), veil usage, and exaggerated proportion to indicate 'the very type of the wandering woman.' Use contrast between long tunic folds and crossing cloak to create visual tension and characterize movement/status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humanisation versus primitive/cosmical import
rubrics_metrics.description: Decide whether the deity is portrayed as an abstract/cosmic force or as human: 'If this figure be indeed Demeter, then the conception of her has become wholly humanised; no trace of the primitive cosmical import of the myth ... remains about it.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humanise divine figures by emphasizing domestic, priestly, or personal traits (weariness, wounded countenance), and downplay mystical or elemental attributes when the intention is to render the deity as a human, relatable character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression of maternity and reconciliation in the seated goddess
rubrics_metrics.description: An enthroned Demeter should show marks of 'reconciliation, enthroned as the glorified mother of all things' with features such as 'delicate plaiting of the tunic about the throat, the formal curling of the hair, and a certain weight of over-thoughtfulness in the brows.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invoke subtle facial details and composed posture to express maternal pensiveness and the idea of a mother who has seen cycles of death and return. The author likens this to Leonardo's sensitive expression of maternity; use restrained, refined signs rather than exaggerated emotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persephone's unearthly, hieratic character and emblems
rubrics_metrics.description: Persephone should appear 'wholly unearthly' — 'compact of sleep, and death, and flowers' — with attributes like the tall tower-like headdress (corn-basket), veil, archaic hands and feet, and stiff folds giving a hieratic character; she often holds the partly consumed pomegranate or a poppy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use iconographic emblems (pomegranate, poppy) and stylized costume/head-dress to signal her chthonic role. The partly consumed pomegranate (one morsel gone) is a nuanced symbol; the poppy evokes narcotic sleep/death and the multitude of seeds as fertility/resurrection. Stiffness and archaic treatment of extremities reinforce ritual, otherworldly dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtle facial gradations to distinguish infernal from Olympian deities
rubrics_metrics.description: Small degrees of expression—'that fulness or heaviness in the brow, as of sleepy people' and 'fine shadows of the little face'—in delicate gradations mark infernal deities from their Olympian kindred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on minute sculptural or descriptive shading (sleepy brows, shadowing of eyes and lips) rather than dramatic gestures to suggest twilight, tranquillity, or infernal associations. These small variations carry semantic weight in classical composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make death attractive, tranquil, and reconciled
rubrics_metrics.description: The image (especially of Persephone) aims 'to lift the old Chthonian gloom ... to connect it with impressions of dignity and beauty, and a certain sweetness ... meant to make men in love, or at least at peace, with death.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When portraying death or underworld themes, seek to ennoble and tranquillize them—use beauty, gentle imagery, and reassuring symbolism so the audience perceives death as a serene, natural part of the cycle rather than only terror.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of myth and symbol as 'pure ideas' to elevate sentiment
rubrics_metrics.description: The myth functions as 'a religion of pure ideas—of conceptions, which having no link on historical fact, yet ... embodied, in adequate symbols, his deepest thoughts concerning the conditions of his physical and spiritual life.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ abstract symbols and mythic imagery to express universal human concerns. Do not feel obliged to historicize every element; the power lies in ideas and their symbolic embodiment to 'elevate and purify' sentiment in literature and art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value and study of local / early art and religion
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigations should attend to 'the early Attic deme-life' and provincial survivals: early, local art and ritual remnants 'are often, indeed, the true maturity of certain amiable artistic qualities' and not merely anticipations of central masterpieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In criticism or creative reconstruction, examine provincial contexts, local rites, minor monuments and early phases rather than focusing solely on canonical centers (e.g., Parthenon). These sources can reveal distinctive practices, original forms, and genuine artistic maturity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evoking provincial/deme life through concrete local detail
rubrics_metrics.description: To render small-town ancient life, use particulars: altars, special worship, markets, relics, sacred images, tombs, local crafts, and seasonal practices (e.g., the by-path to Eleusis, quarries 'like streaks of snow').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground narrative or description in tactile, localized details (markets, offerings of wax/fruit/wool, village chapels, worn pedestals) to convey the variety and intimacy of deme-life. The 'littleness of the physical scene' enhances the intellectual or emotional impression of the culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using mythic figures as cultural symbols (encoding communal sentiment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures like Centaur and Amazon are read as representing 'the regret of Athenians themselves for something that could never be brought to life again'; mythic characters can encode social or political moods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing or analyzing myth, treat legendary personages as symbolic condensations of communal feelings or historical experience—use their presence on friezes or in stories to comment on civic sentiment, loss, or transformation rather than only literal narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone and pacing for the scholarly reader
rubrics_metrics.description: Some material is 'a book for the delighted reading of a scholar, willing to ponder at leisure, to make his way surely, and understand.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a measured, contemplative voice when addressing a scholarly audience: allow for slow development, dense allusion, and attention to nuanced detail rather than brisk, popular exposition.
